places.years: Built 1908 as 西門市場; cinema 1958–1997; reopened 2002-07-26
places.history_en: Built in 1908 as the Ximen public market, designed by Kondo Juro, it joins an octagonal entrance hall to a cross-shaped market hall. After the war the octagon became a stage, the 滬園劇場 opened in 1949, and in 1958 it turned into a cinema, renamed 紅樓戲院 in 1959. From 1976 it showed second-run foreign films and the cinema closed in 1997, the same year the building was assessed as a city monument. A fire on 22 July 2000 destroyed the cross-shaped hall. The octagon reopened on 26 July 2002.

places.history_en: Opened on 22 April 1961 beside the railway on Zhonghua Road, the market was eight connected three-storey blocks named 忠, 孝, 仁, 愛, 信, 義, 和, 平, 1,171 metres long with 1,644 shop units. Each block had its trade: electronics and audio parts in 忠 and 孝, antiques in 仁 and 愛, record shops in 信, restaurants such as 點心世界 and 真北平 in 義, and uniforms and tailoring in 和 and 平. A giant National (國際牌) neon sign stood on the 信 block from 1964 to 1985. The whole row was pulled down in October 1992 for the MRT and the road rebuild.

places.years: Cinemas from the 1950s–60s; 豪華戲院 opened January 1965 and was scheduled to close 2026-05-31
places.history_en: Wuchang Street Section 2 between Kunming Street and Kangding Road became Taipei's cinema row. In the 1950s more than ten theatres opened on this one stretch, and in the 1960s 樂聲, 豪華, 日新, 獅子林, 國王 and 皇后 lined both sides. 豪華戲院 at No. 89 opened in January 1965 with more than 1,500 seats in one hall with upper and lower sections, and showed The Last Emperor in 1988 and Farewell My Concubine in 1993, the year its hall was split in two. As audiences moved east the theatres closed one by one.

places.history_en: Wan Nian stands on the site of the 國際館 cinema, opened in 1936 and renamed 國際戲院 in 1945, which was sold in 1970 and pulled down. The new building, designed by 蔡柏鋒, opened on 6 October 1973 with about 200 shops. Its lower floors sell accessories, clothes, shoes, toys, models and comics, the basement is a food court of long-running stalls, and the fifth floor holds a Tom's World arcade. It once had the 萬年冰宮 skating rink, with a roller-skate area and an ice-skate area.

places.history_en: The block stands where the Higashi Hongan-ji temple once stood. After the war the site was used by the Taiwan Provincial Security Command; the land was put up for sale in 1967 and won by a consortium that included Shin Kong Life. Building work began on 2 February 1977 and the ten-storey Lions' Plaza opened on 30 March 1979, alongside the 六福西門大樓 and the first Lai Lai Department Store. Its cinemas on the fourth and fifth floors, the game arcade on the third and the 金獅大酒樓 dim sum hall on the tenth made it a teenage meeting place.

places.history_en: Lai Lai's Taipei store opened on 25 November 1978 at No. 77, Wuchang Street Section 2, run by the Cathay group, with eight floors above ground and one below. Management passed to the 豐群 group in 1985. It was the big department store of the movie street years, on the same former temple site as Lions' Plaza. Closing was planned for 25 December 2002, but the closing sale sold so well that the last day was pushed back to 10 February 2003. The building now holds an Eslite store and a hotel.

places.history_en: Ay-Chung began in 1975 as a small street stall selling thick rice-flour noodle soup and grew into a shopfront in Ximending. It is known for having no seats and no air conditioning: customers take a bowl and eat it standing in the arcade and the lane outside. Search summaries name the founder as 林明宗 and the address as 峨眉街8-1號, but those two points were not read on a primary page in this research and should be checked.

places.history_en: Fong Da opened in 1956 at No. 42, Chengdu Road. It began as 蜂蜜大王, a honey seller, and moved into tea and coffee sweetened with honey before becoming a coffee house; the present owner 曹世華 took it over from his father. Big glass jars of handmade biscuits stand at the door, the walnut cookie (合桃酥) is its best-known snack, and a German Probat roaster at the back is said to date from the opening. The upstairs once had high-backed lovers' seats. Next door is 南美咖啡, founded the same year.

places.years: Founded 1746 as 艋舺新興宮; at the 成都路 site since 1948; main hall rebuilt 1959-11-29
places.history_en: The temple began in 1746 as 艋舺新興宮 near today's Guiyang Street and Xiyuan Road. In 1943 the Japanese government took the land for a road, and the statues were kept at Longshan Temple. On 7 July 1948 worshippers moved them into the former Kobo-ji, a Shingon Buddhist temple in Ximending. A fire that started in a nearby restaurant later burned the old buildings, a wooden shelter was put up, and the main hall was rebuilt on 29 November 1959. It still keeps a statue of Kobo Daishi beside Mazu. The name 臺北天后宮 dates from 1967.
places.history_zh: 1746年創建於艋舺，原名新興宮。1943年因闢路被拆，神像暫奉龍山寺，1948年遷入西門町原日本弘法寺。後遭大火，1959年11月29日重建正殿。廟內至今供奉弘法大師，是台日信仰並存的少見例子。

places.zh: 西門町徒步區與捷運6號出口廣場
places.en: Ximending Pedestrian Zone and MRT Exit 6 plaza
places.years: Pedestrian zone created 1999; MRT Exit 6 opened 1999-12-24; rainbow crossing 2019-09-25
places.history_en: The pedestrian zone was created in 1999 and a 2008 Taipei Times report called it the largest in the country, with more than three million shoppers a month. A two-weekend car-free trial had already been run in the mid-1980s. MRT Ximen Station opened on 24 December 1999, and Exit 6, on the north side of Chengdu Road at Hanzhong Street, became the station's busiest exit and the usual meeting point. The site was once the Ximen roundabout. Search results date the rainbow crossing in front of the exit to 25 September 2019; that date was not read on a primary page.

Writer 張哲生 described it in 2015 as the lane that took over from movie street as the symbol of Ximending once the cinemas faded. When the first tattoo shops opened there was not found.

events.zh: 五月天成軍五周年西門町小型演唱
events.history_en: In April 2004 the rock band Mayday (五月天) played a small concert in Ximending to mark five years since the band formed, just before setting off on an Asian tour. TVBS headlined its report with fans packing the Red House. For students who had grown up with the band's first albums, it was a rare chance to stand a few metres from five musicians who were already filling stadiums.

events.zh: 周杰倫《七里香》西門町簽唱會
events.en: Jay Chou's album signing jams Ximending
events.history_en: On the afternoon of 14 August 2004 Jay Chou (周杰倫) held a signing for his new album in Ximending and sang the new song 七里香. Central News Agency reported that thousands of fans turned up and traffic around the site knotted up. Signing sessions were how fans met their idols before social media, and this one showed how completely one singer could stop the district.

events.en: Taipei Lantern Festival moves to Ximending
events.history_en: From 4 to 12 February 2017 the Taipei Lantern Festival left its usual home and came to the west side of the city for the first time, lighting up Ximending, 中華路 and the North Gate. The main lantern for the Year of the Rooster was a family of chicks called 小奇雞家族. Young people came for the photos and the night crowds, and the festival has returned to Ximending in many later years.

events.zh: 金馬影展電影公園露天放映《龍貓》
events.history_en: On 10 November 2018 the Golden Horse Film Festival screened Grave of the Fireflies and My Neighbor Totoro back to back under the open sky at Ximending's film park, repeating the way the two films were first shown together in Japan thirty years earlier. Life of Pi followed on 11 November. It was a tribute to director Isao Takahata, who died that year, and it drew a generation raised on Ghibli films.

facts.label: measured

events.zh: 西門6號出口彩虹地景啟用
events.history_en: On 25 September 2019 a six-colour rainbow with the word Taipei was painted on the plaza outside Ximen MRT Exit 6. It marked Taiwan becoming the first place in Asia to legalise same-sex marriage on 17 May that year, and was ready before the Pride parade on 26 October. It quickly became the spot where visitors and students stop for a photo, and it was repainted in 2025.

facts.text: An article updated 2019/09/26 says that 「從9月25日起」 a six-colour rainbow reading 「Taipei」 lies on the plaza in front of 捷運西門站6號出口.
facts.label: measured

facts.text: The same article ties it to same-sex marriage becoming legal on 5月17日 and to the Pride parade on 10月26日, and says city councillors worked with 台北市觀傳局 on it.
facts.label: measured

events.history_en: Through August 2020 the Ximending Back Street Culture Festival took over the film park under the theme 後街製造. There were live vinyl DJ sets and workshops with DJ Chicano, large graffiti pieces with artist Vastar, street dance from the crew 90's bboyz, skateboarding lessons from Delta Skate Supply and Saturday night open-air films. It put the district's street culture, usually tucked in the back lanes, on show for anyone to try.

events.zh: PLAY NOW音樂演唱會「嘻嘻哈哈」
events.en: PLAY NOW hip-hop concert at Exit 6
events.years: 28 February 2021 (date inferred from a 1 March 2021 report)
events.history_en: At the end of February 2021 a free hip-hop show called PLAY NOW EP2 嘻嘻哈哈 was staged on the Exit 6 plaza as part of the 西門PLAY樂購町 shopping campaign. Rapper OSN (高爾宣) led it as campaign ambassador, with 婁峻碩, 陳零九, 呂士軒, 王豔薇 and 陳忻玥 on the bill. Mirror Media reported more than ten thousand visits. The singers were the names filling young listeners' playlists that year.

events.zh: 國際變裝藝術節 × Color Taipei 西門紅樓
events.en: International Drag Festival at the Red House
events.history_en: On 25 October 2025, the day of the 23rd Taiwan Pride parade, drag queens from across Asia were booked to perform at the live house inside the Red House for the International Drag Arts Festival. It was the first year Taipei's tourism department joined the festival, under its Color Taipei programme, and shops around the Red House gave discounts from 22 to 26 October. The Red House squares are the city's best-known LGBT+ meeting place.

facts.text: The same report says shops around 西門紅樓 offered discounts until the 26th, and that the 23rd Taiwan Pride parade on 25 October draws 「超過10萬名國內外旅客」 each year.

events_old_history.zh: 中華商場國際牌霓虹塔拆除
events_old_history.en: The National neon sign comes down
events_old_history.history_en: In 1964 Matsushita Electric put up a giant neon sign for its National brand (國際牌) on the south end of the 信 block of Zhonghua Market. For twenty-one years it was the market's landmark and the glow people saw when they arrived in Ximending at night. It was taken down in 1985 for safety reasons. The day and month were not found.
events_old_history.history_zh: 1964年松下電器在中華商場信棟南面架設巨幅國際牌霓虹招牌，是西門町夜景的代表。1985年因安全問題拆除，確切日期待查。

facts.text: Neon sign installed 1964 on the south face of the 信 block; removed in 1985 for safety reasons.
facts.label: measured

marker.depicts: A standing sign board shaped like the neon tower, with the 國際牌 National sign lit up and a line saying it shone from 1964 to 1985.

events_old_history.location: South end of the 信 block of 中華商場 on 中華路, near 武昌街 (measured for the block; exact spot inferred).
unknowns: Day and month of removal: (unknown — needs CJ)

events_old_history.history_en: Trains used to run at street level along Zhonghua Road, right beside Zhonghua Market, and people waited at level crossings to get into Ximending. The plan to put the tracks underground was approved on 26 July 1979 and work began on 12 July 1983. On 2 September 1989 the first phase opened and was handed to Taiwan Railways, with Premier 李煥 leading the ceremony. Zhonghua Road was widened afterwards.
events_old_history.history_zh: 過去火車沿中華路平面行駛，緊鄰中華商場。鐵路地下化1979年7月26日核定、1983年7月12日動工，1989年9月2日第一期完工通車，由行政院長李煥主持，中華路隨後拓寬。

facts.text: Approved by the Executive Yuan 1979-07-26; groundbreaking 1983-07-12; first phase completed and opened 1989-09-02 with Premier 李煥 presiding.
facts.label: measured

facts.text: 中華商場 stood alongside the railway on 中華路.
facts.label: measured

facts.text: Date the surface tracks and level crossings on 中華路 were physically removed is not given on the page.
facts.label: measured

marker.depicts: A short wall with a level-crossing gate and warning bell, a strip of old track set in the ground, and the date 1989-09-02.

events_old_history.location: On 中華路 at the east edge of the scene, between 中華商場 and the road (inferred position).

photos.shows: Diagram of the stages of undergrounding

unknowns: A photo of the 中華路 level crossing beside the market: (unknown — needs CJ)

events_old_history.history_en: After thirty-one years the eight blocks of Zhonghua Market were pulled down in eleven days. Mayor 黃大洲 gave the order on 20 October 1992 and the 忠 block went first; the 義, 和 and 平 blocks fell on 30 October. The market had declined and the land was needed for the MRT's Ximen Station and the rebuilding of Zhonghua Road. For many Taipei people this is the day old Ximending ended.
events_old_history.history_zh: 1992年10月20日市長黃大洲下令拆除，忠棟最先動工，10月30日義、和、平三棟拆除完畢。啟用31年的中華商場因捷運西門站與中華路改建而走入歷史。

facts.text: Demolition began 1992-10-20 (忠 block) on the order of mayor 黃大洲 and ended 1992-10-30 (義, 和, 平 blocks).
facts.label: measured

facts.text: Reasons: decline of the market, land needed for MRT Ximen Station and the 中華路 redevelopment.
facts.label: measured

marker.depicts: A bronze group of a shopkeeper carrying a folded signboard in front of a half-demolished three-storey block with one of the eight block names (忠) still on the wall.

events_old_history.location: On 中華路 on the market's footprint, east edge of the scene (measured for the market's line).

events_old_history.zh: 紅樓戲院歇業並列為古蹟
events_old_history.en: The Red House cinema closes and becomes a monument
events_old_history.history_en: The 紅樓戲院 had shown films in the octagon since 1958 and second-run foreign films since 1976. By the 1990s it was a faded back-street cinema. It closed in 1997, and on 20 February of that year the building was assessed as a Taipei city monument, which protected it from being torn down. Restoration of the octagon began on 9 June 1998.
events_old_history.history_zh: 紅樓戲院自1958年起在八角樓放映電影，1997年歇業。同年2月20日建築評定為市定古蹟，1998年6月9日八角樓開始整修。

facts.text: Cinema closed in 1997; monument assessment dated 1997-02-20; octagon restoration began 1998-06-09.
facts.label: measured

marker.depicts: A standing board in the shape of an old cinema ticket window with a hand-painted 'last show' poster and the monument plaque date.

events_old_history.location: In front of the Red House octagon, south side of 成都路 (measured).
unknowns: Day and month the cinema closed: (unknown — needs CJ)

events_old_history.zh: 西門町行人徒步區設立
events_old_history.history_en: In 1999 the city closed the core streets of Ximending to cars and made them a pedestrian zone, described in 2008 as the largest in the country, with more than three million shoppers a month. Together with the new MRT station it brought young people back to a district that had lost ground to east Taipei since the 1980s. A three-month trial to extend the zone west to Kangding Road ran from 21 June 2008 and was dropped after shopkeepers protested.
events_old_history.history_zh: 1999年西門町核心街道設為行人徒步區，是全台最大的徒步區，每月逾三百萬人次。它與捷運通車一起，讓1980年代起被東區取代的西門町重新聚集年輕人。

facts.text: The pedestrian zone was created in 1999; largest in the country; over 3 million shoppers a month.
facts.label: measured

facts.text: 2008 trial: extended west from 昆明街 to 康定路 and south from 峨眉街 to 成都路, for three months, weekdays 6pm–11pm and weekends 11am–11pm.
facts.label: measured

facts.text: The 2008 trial ran 2008-06-21 to 2008-09-21 and was suspended after protests; Ximending lost its lead to 東區 in the 1980s and revived with the late-1990s pedestrian zone and the MRT.
facts.label: measured

marker.depicts: A standing board made like a 'pedestrians only' street sign with a no-cars symbol, the year 1999, and a small map of the car-free streets.

events_old_history.location: At the 漢中街 entrance to the zone, just north of the Exit 6 plaza (inferred).
unknowns: Exact date in 1999, the first streets included, and who opened it: (unknown — needs CJ)

events_old_history.history_en: MRT Ximen Station opened on Christmas Eve, 24 December 1999, when the Nangang line reached Ximen and the Banqiao line ran on to Longshan Temple. The station lies under Zhonghua Road, on land cleared when Zhonghua Market came down seven years earlier. The second pair of platforms opened on 31 August 2000 with the Xiaonanmen line. Exit 6 quickly became the station's busiest exit and the front door of Ximending.
events_old_history.history_zh: 捷運西門站於1999年12月24日通車，位於中華路下方，正是七年前拆除中華商場所騰出的土地。2000年8月31日小南門線通車。6號出口成為全站最繁忙的出口，也是西門町的大門。

facts.text: Platforms 1 and 3 opened 1999-12-24 with the Nangang and Banqiao line segments; platforms 2 and 4 opened 2000-08-31 with the Xiaonanmen line.
facts.label: measured

facts.text: 中華路 runs above the station; Exit 6 is the busiest exit.
facts.label: measured

facts.text: 中華商場 was demolished partly to build Ximen Station.
facts.label: measured

marker.depicts: A stand shaped like the Exit 6 entrance canopy with the blue Bannan line colour, an old station name board reading 西門 Ximen, and the date 1999-12-24.

events_old_history.location: At Exit 6, north side of 成都路 at 漢中街 (measured).

events_old_history.zh: 紅樓十字樓大火與八角樓重新開幕
events_old_history.en: The Red House fire and reopening
events_old_history.years: Fire 2000-07-22; octagon reopened 2002-07-26; cross-shaped hall reopened 2004-10-24
events_old_history.history_en: In the early hours of 22 July 2000 a fire destroyed the cross-shaped market hall behind the Red House and about 200 stalls. The octagon, already under restoration, survived. It reopened on 26 July 2002 with the 紙風車 foundation running it as a theatre and tea house. Rebuilding of the cross-shaped hall began on 26 August 2001; it had a trial sale on 3 July 2003 and reopened on 24 October 2004.
events_old_history.history_zh: 2000年7月22日清晨大火燒毀紅樓後方的十字樓與約200個攤位，整修中的八角樓倖存。八角樓於2002年7月26日由紙風車接手重新開幕，十字樓重建後於2004年10月24日重新啟用。

facts.text: Fire in the early morning of 2000-07-22 destroyed the 十字樓 and about 200 market stalls.
facts.label: measured

facts.text: 八角樓 reopened 2002-07-26 operated by 紙風車; 十字樓 groundbreaking 2001-08-26, trial sale 2003-07-03, reopened 2004-10-24.
facts.label: measured

marker.depicts: A low wall of scorched red bricks on one half and clean new bricks on the other, with the two dates 2000-07-22 and 2002-07-26.

events_old_history.location: Behind the Red House octagon, beside the cross-shaped hall, south of 成都路 (measured).
unknowns: Cause of the fire and whether anyone was hurt: (unknown — needs CJ)

events_old_history.en: Lai Lai Department Store's last day
events_old_history.history_en: Lai Lai had stood on movie street since 25 November 1978. It planned to close on 25 December 2002, but so many people came to the closing sale that the last day was pushed back to 10 February 2003. Its end marked the close of the department-store era in Ximending; the building later became an Eslite store and a hotel.
events_old_history.history_zh: 1978年開幕的來來百貨原訂2002年12月25日結束營業，因封館拍賣人潮踴躍，延到2003年2月10日才熄燈，象徵西門町百貨時代的結束。

facts.text: Opened 1978-11-25; closing planned for 2002-12-25 and delayed to 2003-02-10 because of strong closing-sale takings.
facts.label: measured

facts.text: Now 誠品武昌店 and a hotel.
facts.label: measured

marker.depicts: A standing board shaped like a department-store shopping bag with a 'closing sale' banner and the dates 1978–2003.
